disagreements.topic: Does today's group re-rating (Google-Constellation; DOE loan) change 2027-28 EBITDA or fair value?
disagreements.positions: All five: no. Sector sentiment only; DOE uprates arrive 2031-34.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed at primary sources: no change to 2027-28 EBITDA or to fair value. Google-Constellation (Oct 6): 20-year PPA for 890 MW of uprates at 11 Constellation units, first uprate 'by 2028', plus a 15-year 2,700 MW energy supply agreement; Vistra is not mentioned and no price is given. DOE (Oct 5): 'conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion' for uprates and modernization at Beaver Valley, Davis-Besse and Perry (433 MW new capacity), with an option for Comanche Peak uprates; Vistra 'must satisfy certain technical, legal, environmental, and financial conditions' before definitive documents. The 433 MW are the Meta-contracted uprates: delivery begins 'by 2031', full by year-end 2034, with less than 20% of uprate capex by YE2028 (Meta 8-K). Q2 slide 10 already shows growth capex net of expected financing and includes 'PJM nuclear uprates', so the loan affects funding cost after 2028, not 2027-28 EBITDA. The read-through for VST is a higher chance of contracting its open nuclear (bull-case probability), not base-case cash flow. Price action: VST $161.41 (+11.4%) and CEG $307.33 (+14.8%) at ~12:25 ET (Twelve Data quotes), versus a brief close of $159.50.
disagreements.evidence: energy.gov 2026-10-05; googlecloudpresscorner.com 2026-10-06; Vistra-Meta 8-K 2026-01-09; Q2 2026 slides p.10; Twelve Data quotes 2026-10-06.

disagreements.topic: Is consensus CY2027 EPS ($10.42) consistent with the low-end EBITDA ($8.1B) used in the EV leg?
disagreements.positions: agents 1, 2, 4, 5 use $10.42 (agent_4 says it 'looks a few percent above' and cuts the P/E weight to 0.4); agent_3 builds a bridge giving $9.98 at the low end and $10.45 at the $8.3B midpoint.
disagreements.resolution: Agent_3 is right, and the inputs are now verified. With fixed charges below EBITDA calibrated to the 2026 guide midpoint ($7.2B) and 2026 consensus EPS $8.78 (F = 7,200 - (8.78 x 339.5 + 192) / 0.79 = $3.18B), plus ~$0.40B of Cogentrix interest and D&A (judgment: ~5.5% on $3.8B + D&A), 2027E EPS at $8.1B = ((8,100 - 3,584) x 0.79 - 192) / 338.3M = $9.98 (estimate). Using the company's own 2026 guidance D&A $2,150M + interest $1,200M instead gives $9.59. Tax 21% matches guidance ($830-1,000M on $3.93-4.73B pretax). So consensus $10.42 sits at or above the pro forma midpoint, not the low end the CFO pointed to. The EV leg and the P/E leg must use one earnings base, so I put the P/E leg on the bridge: 2028E = ((8,290 - 3,634) x 0.79 - 192) / 332.1M = $10.50; NTM at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x 9.98 + 0.75 x 10.50 = $10.37; x 15.0x = $155.6 (was $164.5). Citation gate (Oct 6), Sep 24 notes: the 424B2 says the ~$1.48B net proceeds of the $1.5B junior subordinated notes ($850M 7.000% Series A + $650M 7.250% Series B, due 2057) go to redeem 'some or all' of the 8.0% Series A and 7.0% Series B preferred ($1.0B each, 10-Q) at their Oct/Dec 2026 reset dates. Base case: both redeemed, so from 2027 preferred dividends fall from $192M to Series C's $42M (476,066 x $1,000 x 8.875%) and fixed charges rise by $135M (notes $850M x 7.000% + $650M x 7.250% = $106.6M, plus ~5.5% on the $0.52B redemption gap = $28.6M, judgment). 2027E = ((8,100 - 3,584 - 135) x 0.79 - 42) / 338.3M = $10.11 (was $9.98); 2028E = ((8,290 - 3,634 - 135) x 0.79 - 42) / 332.1M = $10.63 (was $10.50); NTM = 0.25 x 10.11 + 0.75 x 10.63 = $10.50; x 15.0x = $157.5 (was $155.6). On guidance D&A + interest: ((8,100 - 2,150 - 1,200 - 400 - 135) x 0.79 - 42) / 338.3M = $9.72 (was $9.59). Consensus $10.42 is still above the low-end bridge, by ~3% instead of ~4%.
disagreements.evidence: Q2 release guidance reconciliation (D&A $2,150M, interest $1,200M, tax $830-1,000M); Q2 release income statement (H1 D&A $929M, interest $575M, preferred dividends $96M); XBRL preferred dividends $192M (FY2025); StockAnalysis VST consensus $8.78 / $10.42; Q2 transcript.

It is structural (the CFO attributes 2027's low end to merchant ERCOT exposure; 2028 is only ~72% hedged) and visible in today's prices on both sides of today's move. The premium to the merchant median is only partly justified, by contracted nuclear (Meta 20-yr PPAs on 2,176 MW operating, full delivery by YE2027), the ~94% 2027 hedge and the retail book. So the P/E is held below VST's own 15.31x, and the EBITDA multiple is no higher than its own 10.0x.
